clue.text: Some stars make not one call. It's very odd

indicators.note: something very odd is strange or out of order, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: it's spelt out as the letters of it is, ITS

explanation.surface: Someone is told to phone everyone but one, an instruction they find very strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very odd' rearranges NOT ONE CALL plus ITS; 'make' is a link joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A constellation is a named group of stars seen as a pattern in the night sky.

clue.text: A gemstone displayed without a twitch of eye

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the gemstone's letters surround the twitch

parts.note: the opal is a gemstone with shifting colours
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A jewel shown off to a crowd that stays calm without a flicker of the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'displayed' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical describes things relating to sight or the eye.

clue.text: Very little house in London

definitions.note: the definition is a place in London, a district rather than a description

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
HO is the short form of house, as in a business address

explanation.surface: A tiny cottage tucked away somewhere in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little house' means a shortened house, HO. SOHO is a district of central London known for its nightlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of the West End of the British capital.

clue.text: Having no aim in life, but enduring

definitions.meaning: with no purpose or goal, read cryptically as without an end
lasting for ever, going on without stopping

explanation.surface: A drifter has no purpose in life yet keeps going regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is without a goal (an end); the other is lasting with no finish, as an eternal thing does.

clue.text: Suffered almost terse correspondence

parts.note: to suffer in its old sense is to allow, as in suffer the little children, giving let

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone put up with mail that was nearly curt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffered' here is the old sense of allowed, LET; 'almost' cuts the last E from TERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence is the mail people write and send each other.

clue.text: Kind of shirt a person will find sound

parts.note: a T-shirt is a kind of shirt named by its letter
one means a person, as in one should be careful

explanation.surface: Somebody looking for the right style of shirt in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A tone is a musical sound or note of a particular pitch.

clue.text: There can be no let-up for the really well-off!.

indicators.note: can be signals that the letters of the words given can be turned into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: The idle rich are told they will get no rest from their wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' signals that NO LET-UP can be rearranged; 'There', 'for' and 'the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means wealthy and showing luxury, like the very rich.

clue.text: Fed-up about derision, a virtuous man carried seating

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for fed-up goes round the jeering and the saint together
carried says the jeering and the saint are borne inside the word for fed-up

parts.note: fed up means sick, as in sick of it
hooting is jeering and derisive noise
ST is the abbreviation of saint, a virtuous man

explanation.surface: A grumpy saint, mocked by a crowd, is carried off to a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried' just reinforces the container: the jeering and the saint are borne inside. A shooting stick is a walking stick that unfolds into a seat, used at outdoor events.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting stick is a pointed stick whose handle opens out to form a seat.

clue.text: Wobbly legs mean mares being 17 across

definitions.note: the definition is the answer to 17 across, a bad feeling or sickness

indicators.note: wobbly means unsteady and moving about, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Unsteady horses are described as ill, legs shaking under them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wobbly' rearranges LEGS MEAN MARES; 17 across is ILLNESS, so the definition is a sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: German measles, or rubella, is a contagious viral disease causing a rash.

clue.text: Didn't at all like the church interior, so came out

indicators.note: interior means the church goes inside the other word

parts.note: to hate something is not to like it at all

explanation.surface: A visitor disliked the church's decor and walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came out' is the definition, as a chick does from an egg; 'so' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A chick that has hatched has broken out of its egg.

clue.text: Not retiring-certain to find a distinctive hair-style

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word before it is read in reverse

parts.note: certain means sure

explanation.surface: An outgoing person is sure to get noticed with a striking haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen hides a break: 'Not retiring' is wordplay, not a description of a shy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown worn by monks, a very recognisable haircut.

clue.text: Part of the initiation ceremony at one time

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A recollection of some section of an induction ritual from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly or at some point in the past, as in a story that begins long ago.

clue.text: Left flat in Scotland

definitions.note: the definition points to a place in Scotland rather than describing it

parts.note: flat means level or even

explanation.surface: Someone has moved out of their apartment north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a home but means level, EVEN. Leven is a town on the Fife coast and a loch in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Leven is a Fife town and the name of a Scottish loch.

clue.text: Ray's broad grin

explanation.surface: A man called Ray has a big smile on his face.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft of light is one sense; to smile widely is another, also the same word.

clue.text: Rise and dress

definitions.meaning: to get out of bed or stand up
an outfit, often an unusual one

explanation.surface: An instruction to stand up and put clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb out of bed is one sense; an outfit or costume is the noun sense.

clue.text: A chaplain has to go on foot with soldiers

parts.note: to pad is to walk softly
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: An army chaplain must walk alongside the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps; 'has to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the services' name for a military priest.

clue.text: Bad feeling

parts.note: reads as resentment or animosity, but here means feeling unwell, being sick

explanation.surface: Resentment or ill will between people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad feeling' suggests hostility; read literally it is feeling poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sick is literally feeling bad in body.

clue.text: Quarter some with an old Greek

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass
part means some of something

explanation.surface: Someone shares lodgings with an ancient Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarter' looks like housing but is a compass point, S.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spartan was a citizen of Sparta, a city state of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Action gets results at the riverside

indicators.note: results reads as the result of reworking the word before it, giving a new arrangement

parts.note: the Ure is a Yorkshire river, placed at the side of the other letters

explanation.surface: Doing something produces outcomes down by the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'results' rearranges GETS into GEST; the URE is a river in Yorkshire, added at the side.
explanation.definitionFit: A gesture is a movement or deed done to show feeling.

clue.text: Treats possibly about fifty for shock

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the numeral
possibly says the word before it could become something else, a rearrangement

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty sweets might come as a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TREATS into STARTE; 'about' puts it around L.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to give them a sudden fright.

clue.text: Obscure egghead cuts another

parts.note: the head of egg is its first letter, E
clips means cuts, as with shears
another egghead, a second E

explanation.surface: A clever person snips at a rival intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like a clever person but means the head of egg, E; 'another' gives a second E.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to hide or block the light of something, outshining it.

clue.text: A body of seamen imprisoned for murder

annotationWithheld.why: A body of seamen imprisoned for murder (7): A + RN must sit inside CAGE, but 'imprisoned' would have to give CAGE and signal the insertion at once, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: A body of seamen imprisoned for murder

clue.text: The buccaneer's coarse-sounding song

indicators.note: sounding means the word before is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the word coarse said aloud matches the first part
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A pirate's rough, vulgar shanty.
explanation.walkthrough: COARSE said out loud gives the start, then AIR (song).
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a pirate, especially one raiding the Mediterranean coasts.

clue.text: Calculating the value of 5 down

parts.note: 5 down is mail or correspondence, but here means the symbols x and y whose values maths works out

explanation.surface: Working out what some mail is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 down is LETTERS: the clue reads as valuing post, but means finding unknowns written as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is the branch of mathematics using symbols to stand for unknown numbers.

clue.text: Drop the rent

definitions.meaning: a falling bead of water from the eye

explanation.surface: A tenant gives up paying the rent.
explanation.definitionFit: A weeping drop and a rip in fabric share one spelling.

clue.text: Regal eccentric getting a black look

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd monarch gives someone an angry stare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges REGAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A glare is a fierce, angry stare, a dark look.

clue.text: Encourages the production of food

definitions.meaning: what hens lay, which people eat

explanation.surface: Someone supports the farming industry.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge on is one sense; what hens lay for breakfast is the other.

clue.text: Unusual hat — one made for an Oriental

indicators.note: unusual signals the word after it is put in an odd new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A strange hat crafted for someone from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges HAT; 'one' gives I, and 'made for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thai is a person from Thailand in South-East Asia.

clue.text: The Italian turning on a beast

indicators.note: turning means the Italian word is read backwards

parts.note: il is the Italian word for the
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian man rounds on an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Italian' looks like a person but means the Italian word for the, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion is a big cat, a large wild animal.

clue.text: Hastily grab the sauce

definitions.meaning: a tomato condiment, usually spelt ketchup

explanation.surface: Someone snatches up the ketchup bottle in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To snatch up in a hurry is one reading; the other is a variant spelling of the tomato condiment.

clue.text: A note written by expert will be most pleasant

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale
able means skilled, expert

explanation.surface: A message from a specialist is always welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: MI is the third note of the do-re-mi scale; 'written by' and 'will be most' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiable means friendly and good-natured.

clue.text: New trend in a mere a large stretch of water

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh fashion appears on a small lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges TREND IN A MERE A; a mere is a small lake, part of the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean is the sea between Europe and Africa.
